headline: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed major capital proposals, including a $1.82 million smart water meter project and water infrastructure repairs.
synopsis: The Capital Improvement and Planning Committee reviewed FY28 capital requests and multi-year forecasts from the Department of Public Works and Water Enterprise. Priorities included an estimated $1.82 million smart water meter system to curb water loss, $700,000 for state-mandated water tank rehabilitation, and $823,000 in potential soil remediation costs. The committee also discussed heavy vehicle replacements and the possible establishment of a fee-supported stormwater utility enterprise fund. Additionally, members received status updates on the Neary School renovation design and Community Preservation Act grant funding for Fay Park.

highlights.title: DPW and Water FY28 capital requests and multi-year plan
highlights.why: The DPW presented requests including a $1.82 million smart water meter conversion, $700,000 for state-mandated water tank repairs, and an estimated $823,000 for soil remediation at the former Atwood tank site.

highlights.title: Neary School Building Committee update
highlights.why: The preferred path forward is a renovation of the existing Neary school with a new full-sized gymnasium, with an architect briefing and updated cost estimates scheduled for mid-November.

highlights.title: Fay Park project CPA funding status
highlights.why: A grant will cover half of the Fay Park improvement costs, while the remaining matching funds are being requested through Community Preservation Act funds rather than general tax revenue.
